title: PAR-14 checked EED byte-to-bit cursor
mode: Source audit and generated arithmetic fast slice
scope: Inspect parser-relevant count/length and byte-to-bit arithmetic in the current EED path.
Replace an unchecked input-derived byte-position conversion with checked arithmetic.
Add bounded integer-only controls and run only the owning fast tests.

sources.revision: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, §28, reviewed 2026-10-20
sources.observed: EED directly follows an entity handle and consists of repeated application chunks whose bit-short length bounds the application handle and data items. This supports checking cursor arithmetic against the enclosing bit boundary; it does not define a platform-sized DWG file limit.

localEvidence: src/intern/dwgreader.cpp eedCurrentBit/eedHasBits/readEedHandle use an absolute bit cursor for bounded EED parsing.
src/intern/dwgsafety.h now provides checked byte-to-bit position conversion using checked multiply and add.
tests/hardening_tests.cpp tests maximum representable bit position, multiplication overflow, and invalid bit offset.
tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp contains existing bounded EED chunk and following-entity controls.
planChanges: Record the unchecked EED absolute bit-cursor arithmetic as a confirmed PAR-14 local gap and close this implementation slice.
Require checked multiplication/addition before comparing a byte-derived bit offset with a DWG object/EED boundary.
Self-unblock to the next source-backed parser arithmetic expression and keep validation limited to the owning fast targets.
limitations: The overflow case is tested at the arithmetic helper boundary; an impractically large sparse DWG was not created.
No full suite, peer implementation, native CAD application, or ACIS kernel was run.
No external drawing fixture was downloaded or added.
